facts: Every binary package has three dimensions: what it is, which version, and which platform build. [L6]
OCX collapses all three into one identifier that resolves, verifies and installs the right binary without extra flags. [L8]
An OCI tag is a mutable pointer, since the distribution spec offers no notion of tag stability. [L12]
The _build suffix, typically a UTC timestamp, signals that the publisher will not re-push, by convention only. [L22]
OCI tags reject plus signs, so OCX uses underscore as the build separator and every version is a valid tag. [L25]
Typing a plus sign anyway is accepted and normalized to underscore automatically. [L27]
A build-tagged reference stays put on index refresh, while rolling tags advance to the latest build. [L32]
Any tag, including build-tagged ones, can be overwritten by its publisher. [L39]
Installed binaries live at a path derived from their SHA-256 digest, so the tag used to install them is irrelevant. [L42]
A digest reference gives absolute reproducibility without any index. [L44]
Variants describe how a binary was built rather than where it runs, and the user chooses one rather than auto-detection. [L49]
Docker-style tag suffixes are ambiguous with semver prereleases, since 3.12-alpha and 3.12-slim look alike. [L54]
OCX uses a variant-prefix format, so debug-3.12.5 is unambiguous because versions always start with a digit. [L57]
The debug-3 tag names the latest debug variant in the 3.x series. [L63]
Rolling tags cascade within their own variant track, and variants never cross. [L67]
Aliasing onto the bare track is opt-in through package push with the default flag. [L69]
The OCI platform variant is a CPU sub-architecture chosen automatically, while OCX variants are chosen by the user. [L71]
Publishers maintain the tag hierarchy, re-pointing rolling ancestors only when a release is latest at each level. [L77]
Publishing 3.27.5 updates 3.27 but not 3 or latest, since the 3.28 series is still ahead. [L91]
The push cascade flag re-points all rolling ancestors in one command. [L98]
A transient error during a cascade can leave an alias pointing at an older build, and resolution does not notice. [L101]
An image index lets several platform builds share one tag, and the installer selects the matching build. [L111]
A universal build with no platform field is used as a fallback. [L121]
Any package can be pinned by digest, which needs no lockfile and no registry query. [L139]
